newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US T-bond vols sag, May expires quietly.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US T-bond vols sag, May expires quietly.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond futures sagged in the face of weekend time decay pressure as the underlying bond market drifted marginally higher in listless trading, dealers said.
May T-bond futures options on the Chicago Board of Trade expired at midday without causing much turbulence in the market, they added.

"We've been trading around the 107-handle for quite a while (in June futures), so there was no run to a strike," said a trader for a brokerage firm at CBOT. "Plus, it's a serial option, not quarterly."
However, he added that one firm bought 3,000 contracts of May 108 calls early in the session and that hedging by counterparties of that trade contributed to June futures' climb above 108-00.
The futures contract stood at 108-2/32 in late trade, up 7/32 on the day.
Implied volatility for June T-bond futures options fell about 0.2 point to around 8.2 percent.
June volatility was likely to stay subdued for a while as June contracts expire on May 16 and do not cover the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee meeting, traders said.
September volatility was steady at 8.9 percent. Further out the curve, one firm was said to have bought 2,000 contracts of deep out-of-the-money December 120 calls.
Traders said growing optimism about the bond market's near-term outlook, with bonds enjoying their first weekly gains since mid-February, was likely to dampen bounces in volatilities next week.

In Eurodollar options, volatilities were holding in well for a Friday as the underlying market has had moderately good intraday movement relative to the historically low implied volatility levels, traders said.
"The market's been moving around enough to keep volatilities from slipping any further," said a brokerage trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.

"Once you get down to certain levels (in implied volatilities), you can pay the rent (premiums) with just a little bit of movement," he added, referring to profits to be eeked out in futures transactions by delta-hedging volatility players.
Implied volatilities for September and December Eurodollar futures options on CME were virtually unchanged at around 10.2 and 11.8 percent respectively.
September futures were up three basis points, while the 1998 contracts gained about six basis points.
Among the biggest trades, one investment bank was said to have bought 4,000 contracts of short-May 93.00 puts, which are options that expire shortly but priced off June 1998 futures.

A German firm was seen buying 1,500 lots of September 93.75 puts, while a third firm traded 1,000 legs of September 93.75/94.00/94.25 call "Christmas tree", buying the 93.75 strike and selling 94.00 and 94.25.
